title: UT Martin Skyhawk rodeo teams begin season under new head coach Ken Mason
text:
UT Martin Skyhawk rodeo teams begin season under new head coach Ken Mason
M. M. Gaines
The University of Tennessee at Martin Skyhawk rodeo teams will begin their 2026-27 season on Sept. 17 as they travel to Marshall, Missouri, for a rodeo hosted by Missouri Valley College. This event marks the start of the first UT Martin rodeo under new head coach Ken Mason, who officially became the program's sixth all-time leader on July 1.
Mason, a 1998 Skyhawk graduate, returns to Missouri Valley College after previously guiding both men's and women's teams to a combined 19 Ozark Region titles, three reserve national team championships, and five individual national champions from 2005 through 2026. The UT Martin roster features 29 returning student-athletes from last year—14 cowboys and 15 cowgirls. Among them are four men's returners who ranked in the top 15 in the Ozark Region in various events during the previous season: Cooper Stone, Owen Larrick, Daniel Wilder, and Bentley Anthony. On the women's side, Kylie Jo Castor (barrel racing), Bekah Legan (breakaway roping), and Drew Thomas (breakaway roping) each finished among the region's top 15 in their respective events.
Mason has also recruited 31 newcomers for this season's roster—including 16 men and 15 women—with thirteen having collegiate experience last year; eleven of those bring Ozark Region experience and ten competed under Mason at Missouri Valley College. Notable additions include Judd Pope (third nationally with regional-high points in saddle bronc riding), Collin Roland (third in region for bareback riding), Creek Caldwell (third regionally for saddle bronc riding), Tate Williams (fifth regionally for tie down roping), Ethan Archer (sixth regionally for saddle bronc riding), Owen Prince (seventh regionally for bareback riding), Kade Parrish (eighth regionally for bareback riding), Kate Brisbane (fourth regionally for goat tying), and Hailey Donald (eighth regionally for goat tying).
"I couldn't be more excited for the season to start," Mason said. "We've been practicing roping calves and tying goats at 5:30 in the morning and there's been more enthusiasm and drive at that time of day than there is in the afternoon. UT Martin already had a talented roster with several timed-event kids and a really good women's roster then we brought in some roughstock guys that are super competitive. It's going to be a well-rounded, balanced team."
The Skyhawks' fall schedule includes five rodeos: West Alabama from Sept. 24-26; Arkansas-Monticello from Oct. 1-3; Missouri State-West Plains' inaugural event Oct. 8-10; Murray State Nov. 19-21; with spring dates yet to be announced except for UT Martin's own Spring College Rodeo set April 8-10 at Ned McWherter Agricultural Complex. The College National Finals Rodeo will take place June 13-19 in Casper, Wyo.
